Subject: MSA + Order Form: Limitation of liability — proposed approach

Hi Samir / BrightRetail team,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, I’m attaching a clean redline of the MSA and an Order Form with a short matrix comparing cap options. High level: we want to keep the commercial terms simple while protecting Redwood against open-ended exposure.

Key options we put into the document for your review:
- Aggregate contract cap = greater of (12 months of fees) or $500k (Redwood preference: standard commercial approach for SaaS)
- Alternative multiple approach = 1x / 3x of fees (negotiable depending on term & commitment)
- Annualized vs total contract-wide cap (we prefer total contract cap for predictability)
- Consequential damages excluded; limited carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity; security/data-breach carve-out limited to direct remediation and regulatory fines (subject to insurance limits)

Ask: can you confirm which of these three levers (base amount, multiplier, annualization) BrightRetail prefers to prioritize? If useful, we can run a short one-pager showing $-impact under each option for the first 24 months of the expected volume.

Attachments: RDW_BrightRetail_MSA_redline_v1.pdf; Cap-structure-comparison-table.pdf

Proposed next step: 30 min sync tomorrow or Wednesday to land on one approach so legal can produce a counter-redline.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Limitation of liability — proposed approach

Marissa,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the matrix. I’ve looped in our legal and procurement teams. Initial feedback from procurement: cost impact is clear, but legal flagged the following concerns:

- They’re uncomfortable with Redwood’s proposed aggregate-only cap. Our playbook typically prefers an annualized cap or a per-incident floor to avoid one-off catastrophic exposure concentrated in a single contract year.
- They suggested a counter that’s the greater of $500k or 3x fees (we’d need a simple rationale on why 3x is commercially defensible for Redwood).
- Data-related damages are sensitive here given our customer base; legal wants explicit carve-outs for regulatory fines and third-party claims tied to data breach.

Can you put together a 1-paragraph commercial rationale for the multiplier approach (e.g., why 3x vs 1x, and when Redwood would accept annualization)? Also open to a brief call to align.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Procurement, BrightRetail
samir.patel@brightretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Limitation of liability — proposed approach

Samir — quick reply with our commercial rationale and a compromise path: 

Rationale (short): our standard cap is calibrated to the churn-adjusted annual revenue Redwood expects to receive from the account and the practical limit of recoverable damages in cloud services (implementation costs, lost margin tied to grossly negligent outages). A multiplier (e.g., 3x fees) provides protection for customers in case of severe sustained failures while allowing Redwood to underwrite the risk (via SLA credits, monitoring, and insurance) without pricing to unlimited liability.

Compromise proposal (practical):
- Per-incident / annual floor: If BrightRetail requires an annualized mechanism, we’ll accept an annual cap equal to 1.5x annual fees with an overall aggregate cap equal to 4x total fees over the contract term.
- Alternative: If BrightRetail insists on a higher per-incident dollar floor, we can accept $2M per-incident with an aggregate cap of 2x fees.
- Carve-outs: consequential and lost profits remain excluded; carve-outs for data breach should be narrowly tailored to direct remediation costs and regulatory penalties (we will require limits and offsets with insurance proceeds).

Attached: OrderForm_Fees_comparison_v2.xlsx (simple model showing $ impact for 1x /1.5x /3x across expected usage).

If this looks directionally acceptable I can ask Legal Ops to draft the specific language (examples attached in the redline). Happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow before your internal CFO review.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: BrightRetail Legal <contracts@brightretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightretail.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 15:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Limitation of liability — proposed approach

Marissa / Samir,

Thanks — we reviewed the redline and the spreadsheet. A few legal comments to keep the drafting tight before we escalate to CFO/tax: 

1) Clause refs: please confirm MSA §10.2 (Limitation) and §12.4 (Indemnities) — we’ve added inline comments in your PDF redline.
2) For data-breach carve-out: BrightRetail cannot agree to unlimited recovery for regulatory fines. We propose removing regulatory fines from carve-outs; instead, allow recovery up to per-incident cap subject to insurance offsets and mandatory breach notification/forensics cooperation.
3) Per-incident vs aggregate: Our commercial team prefers per-incident floor of $2M with an aggregate cap at 3x fees. This balances our exposure and preserves remediation funds for discrete events.
4) IP indemnity: we’ll keep current language but require Redwood to accept infringement indemnity limited to claims caused by Redwood’s deliverables (not customer content).

We’ll need an internal signoff process (procurement + legal + CFO). If you can accept the per-incident $2M / aggregate 3x fees trade, we can move to final contract review.

Regards,
BrightRetail Legal (on behalf of BrightRetail Inc.)
contracts@brightretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Limitation of liability — proposed approach

Internal summary / recommendation: 

1) BrightRetail legal wants: per-incident $2M floor + aggregate 3x fees. They’ve tied escalation to CFO approval.
2) Our prior ask: aggregate-first or multiplier; compromise of per-incident $2M / aggregate 2x fees (Marissa proposal) is probably the most defendable. Trade-offs: higher per-incident floor increases our underwriting exposure and likely impacts price.

Recommended commercial counter for approval: accept per-incident $2M with an aggregate cap of 2.5x annual fees for the initial 12 months, with the following offsets/controls: 
- SLA credits formula: meaningful uptime credits capped at 25% of monthly invoice for qualifying incidents
- Insurance certificate: BrightRetail to accept our certificate of cyber insurance (minimum $5M limit) in lieu of unlimited carve-outs for regulatory fines
- Joint post-incident review and remediation plan (to limit downstream exposure)

Action items: 
- Laura: confirm accounting impact on deal economics if we accept 2.5x (vs 2x) — need quick P&L delta.
- Stephanie: have Legal Ops prepare the specific redline language for the per-incident/aggregate combo and the SLA-credit offset.
- Karthik: please weigh in on risk tolerance and whether we can accept the insurance-based compromise (I will need a short note from you for sales deck).

If we’re aligned I’ll propose the compromise to Samir and BrightRetail Legal today and see if we can lock CFO signoff before the end of the week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
